about.en:
TEDxBritish University Georgia is an independently organised TEDx event licensed by TED and listed in TED's official TEDx events directory as a 'University' event. It takes place on 27 November 2026 in Tbilisi, organised by Levan Gurgenidze, with the organiser address at 92 Vepkhistkaosani Street, Tbilisi.

TEDx university events combine short live talks by students, academics and local professionals with recorded TED Talks, followed by networking. TED lists this event as open to the public, so secondary-school and university students can attend as audience members; speaker and volunteer places are decided by the organising team.

It is a low-barrier way to hear new ideas, meet people from Tbilisi's university community and, for those who want to speak, a chance to get on the path to giving a TEDx talk.

en: Official TEDx event licensed by TED
Open to the public according to TED's listing
Talks by students, academics and local professionals

eligibility.en: Open to the public. Best suited to university and senior secondary-school students in Tbilisi; most talks are expected in English or Georgian.

en: Open the event's page on ted.com (TEDx events, Georgia) to confirm the date and venue
Contact the organising team listed on the TED page (or the host school/university) to ask for a seat
If you want to speak or volunteer, ask the organisers about speaker and volunteer calls well before the date
Arrive on the day with your confirmation; talks may later be published on the TEDx YouTube channel

costs.en: TED's listing does not mention a ticket price; TEDx university events are usually free or low-cost. Confirm with the organisers. Travel is at your own cost.

score_reason: Real, dated and open to the public, but a single evening with few published details.

about.en:
TEDxIB European School is a TEDx 'Youth' event, licensed by TED, hosted by the European School in Tbilisi (2 Irine Skhirtladze Street), an International Baccalaureate school. TED's official events directory lists it for 20 November 2026, organised by Keti Nachkebia with co-organiser Tea Siradze.

TEDx Youth events put school students on stage: pupils prepare and deliver short talks, often coached by teachers, alongside guest speakers. The event is listed as open to the public, so students from other schools and families can attend.

For a secondary-school student it is a chance to see peers give polished talks in English, and a model for anyone thinking of starting a TEDx Youth licence at their own school.

Hosted by an IB World School in Tbilisi

In the TEDx Youth format, secondary-school students research, write and rehearse short talks and present them alongside invited speakers. The event is marked as open to the public, so students from other schools can come to watch and network.

With the date set months ahead, it is also a realistic target for students who want to ask the organisers about volunteering or speaking opportunities.

org: UNDP Georgia and OHCHR (EU-UN joint project 'Human Rights for All')

name.en: Human Rights Winter School for Youth 2026 (UNDP, OHCHR, EU)
name.ka: ადამიანის უფლებების ზამთრის სკოლა ახალგაზრდებისთვის 2026 (UNDP, OHCHR, EU)
name.ar: المدرسة الشتوية لحقوق الإنسان للشباب 2026 (UNDP وOHCHR والاتحاد الأوروبي)

deadline_note: The EU in Georgia announcement (27 Oct 2026) gives a 10 November 2026 deadline; the EU NEIGHBOURS east listing shows 14 November as closing date. Apply by 10 November to be safe. Venue city not stated.

summary.en: A fully funded six-day winter school on human rights for 18-24-year-old students and graduates in Georgia, run by UNDP and OHCHR under an EU-funded project. Travel and accommodation are covered and graduates receive a certificate.
summary.ka: სრულად დაფინანსებული ექვსდღიანი ზამთრის სკოლა ადამიანის უფლებებზე საქართველოში მცხოვრები 18-24 წლის სტუდენტებისა და კურსდამთავრებულებისთვის, რომელსაც UNDP და OHCHR ევროკავშირის მიერ დაფინანსებული პროექტის ფარგლებში ატარებენ. მგზავრობა და საცხოვრებელი დაფარულია, მონაწილეები სერტიფიკატს იღებენ.
summary.ar: مدرسة شتوية ممولة بالكامل لمدة ستة أيام حول حقوق الإنسان للطلاب والخريجين في جورجيا بعمر 18-24 عامًا، تنظمها UNDP وOHCHR ضمن مشروع يموله الاتحاد الأوروبي. تُغطّى تكاليف السفر والإقامة ويحصل المشاركون على شهادة.

about.en:
The Human Rights Winter School is organised by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) within the EU-UN joint project 'Human Rights for All'. It runs from 29 November to 4 December 2026 and covers human rights in a democratic society, human-rights protection institutions and their challenges, freedom of expression, the right to privacy and personal-data protection.

The programme mixes lectures, discussions, presentations and group exercises, with practical work on communication and presentation skills. It is for students and recent graduates aged 18-24 from law, social sciences, political science and humanities programmes at accredited Georgian universities; applicants from regional universities are particularly welcome. Teaching is in Georgian.

Organisers fully cover transport and accommodation, and everyone who completes the programme gets a certificate, which makes it a strong, free addition to a CV for careers in law, policy or international organisations.

en: Fully funded: transport and accommodation covered
Run by UNDP and OHCHR with EU funding
Certificate of completion

eligibility.en: Students and graduates aged 18-24 of law, social sciences, political sciences or humanities at accredited higher-education institutions in Georgia, with good Georgian and able to attend the whole programme. Regional-university applicants are encouraged.

en: Prepare a CV and a motivation letter of no more than 300 words (your human-rights experience, why you want to attend, how you will use it)
Complete the registration form linked from the EU in Georgia announcement
Submit before 10 November 2026
Shortlisted applicants are contacted by UNDP (contact: ana.kvernadze@undp.org)

costs.en: Free. Transport and accommodation are fully covered by the organisers.

score_reason: Fully funded UN/EU programme with a near, clear deadline; Georgian-language only.

org: UNDP Georgia with EU funding ('Circular Economy: Waste Reduction and Recycling for Citizens' Health')

name.en: Young Content Creators Call: Waste Reduction and Recycling Campaign (EU and UNDP Georgia)
name.ka: ახალგაზრდა კონტენტ-კრეატორების კონკურსი: ნარჩენების შემცირებისა და გადამუშავების კამპანია (EU და UNDP საქართველო)
name.ar: دعوة لصنّاع المحتوى الشباب: حملة تقليل النفايات وإعادة التدوير (الاتحاد الأوروبي وUNDP جورجيا)

deadline_note: Deadline 1 November 2026 per the EU in Georgia announcement of 6 Oct 2026; very short window left.

summary.en: The EU and UNDP are selecting up to 12 young content creators in Georgia (18-29) to run three-month social-media campaigns on waste reduction and recycling, with training, mentoring and a GEL 3,000 award each. No large following is needed.
summary.ka: ევროკავშირი და UNDP საქართველოში არჩევენ 12-მდე ახალგაზრდა კონტენტ-კრეატორს (18-29 წ.), რომლებიც სამთვიან სოციალური მედიის კამპანიებს ჩაატარებენ ნარჩენების შემცირებასა და გადამუშავებაზე; მათ ელით ტრენინგი, მენტორობა და 3000 ლარიანი ჯილდო. დიდი აუდიტორია საჭირო არ არის.
summary.ar: يختار الاتحاد الأوروبي وUNDP حتى 12 صانع محتوى شابًا في جورجيا (18-29 عامًا) لتنفيذ حملات على وسائل التواصل لمدة ثلاثة أشهر حول تقليل النفايات وإعادة التدوير، مع تدريب وإرشاد ومنحة قدرها 3000 لاري لكل منهم. لا يشترط وجود عدد كبير من المتابعين.

about.en:
Under the EU-funded project 'Circular Economy: Waste Reduction and Recycling for Citizens' Health', UNDP and the European Union invite young bloggers, vloggers and social-media creators from across Georgia to design and run campaigns on waste reduction, battery and e-waste recycling, packaging and sorting, reuse and repair, and responsible consumption.

Up to 12 participants will be selected. Between January and March 2027 they take part in training and mentoring, then create and publish the agreed content on their own TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, X or other channels. Each receives a GEL 3,000 implementation award. Creativity and understanding of your audience matter more than follower count.

It is open to residents of Georgia aged 18-29, with young women and men from all regions and from under-served communities particularly encouraged. It is a paid, portfolio-building project for anyone interested in environmental communication or digital media.

en: GEL 3,000 implementation award per selected creator
Training and mentoring from UNDP's EU-funded project
No minimum follower count

eligibility.en: Residents of Georgia aged 18-29 who create content on any social-media platform. Applicants from all regions and diverse communities are encouraged.

en: Read the call on the EU in Georgia or UNDP Georgia page
Prepare a campaign idea and links to your social-media channels
Apply through UNDP Georgia's call page before 1 November 2026
Selected creators are trained and run campaigns January-March 2027

costs.en: Free to apply. Selected participants receive a GEL 3,000 award to deliver their campaign, plus training and mentoring.

score_reason: Paid, EU/UN-backed and open to all of Georgia, but the deadline is 1 November.

org: Faculty of Humanities, Ivane Javakhishvili Tbilisi State University (TSU)

name.ka: სტუდენტთა სამეცნიერო კონფერენცია „თსუ 109“ (2027, თბილისის სახელმწიფო უნივერსიტეტი)
name.ar: المؤتمر العلمي الطلابي 'TSU 109' لعام 2027 (جامعة تبليسي الحكومية)

deadline_note: TSU announcement (26 Oct 2026): abstracts by 20 December 2026; conference 11-12 February 2027.

summary.en: An annual student research conference marking Tbilisi State University's 109th anniversary, held on 11-12 February 2027. Students submit a one-page abstract by 20 December 2026 and present for 15 minutes in Georgian.
summary.ka: თბილისის სახელმწიფო უნივერსიტეტის დაარსების 109-ე წლისთავისადმი მიძღვნილი ყოველწლიური სტუდენტური სამეცნიერო კონფერენცია, რომელიც 2027 წლის 11-12 თებერვალს გაიმართება. სტუდენტები ერთგვერდიან თეზისს 2026 წლის 20 დეკემბრამდე წარადგენენ და 15-წუთიან მოხსენებას ქართულად აკეთებენ.
summary.ar: مؤتمر بحثي طلابي سنوي بمناسبة الذكرى 109 لتأسيس جامعة تبليسي الحكومية، يُعقد يومي 11-12 فبراير 2027. يقدّم الطلاب ملخصًا من صفحة واحدة قبل 20 ديسمبر 2026 ويعرضون أبحاثهم لمدة 15 دقيقة باللغة الجورجية.

about.en:
The 'TSU 109' Student Scientific Conference is organised every year by the Faculty of Humanities of Ivane Javakhishvili Tbilisi State University to mark the university's founding; the 2027 edition is the fifth. It takes place at TSU in Tbilisi on 11-12 February 2027.

Students send a thesis (abstract) of at most one page (about 250 words, Sylfaen 12, 1.5 spacing) together with a written statement from a professor or supervisor confirming it meets the conference's academic requirements. Accepted speakers present for 15 minutes, followed by 10 minutes of discussion. The working language is Georgian.

It is a first step into academic presenting for undergraduate and master's students, and a line on a CV that graduate programmes and scholarship committees value.

en: Annual conference tied to TSU's founding anniversary
15-minute talk plus 10-minute discussion
Free to take part

eligibility.en: Students able to present research in Georgian, with a supporting statement from a professor or supervisor. The announcement is addressed to TSU students and does not say whether students of other universities are accepted; ask the organisers.

en: Write a one-page abstract (max. 250 words, Sylfaen 12, 1.5 line spacing)
Get a written statement from your professor or supervisor approving the abstract
Email both to javakhishvili_students@tsu.ge by 20 December 2026
If accepted, present on 11-12 February 2027 at TSU (contact: Dr Nino Popiashvili)

score_reason: Dated and free, but Georgian-language and aimed mainly at TSU students.

org: Institute of the History and Theory of Art, Tbilisi State University (TSU)

name.en: Student Conference 'Man and Culture Across Epochs' 2026 (TSU Institute of Art History)
name.ka: სტუდენტური სამეცნიერო კონფერენცია „ადამიანი და კულტურა ეპოქათა შორის“ 2026 (თსუ)
name.ar: المؤتمر الطلابي 'الإنسان والثقافة عبر العصور' 2026 (معهد تاريخ الفن، جامعة تبليسي الحكومية)

deadline_note: TSU announcement (22 Oct 2026): abstracts by 10 November 2026; programme published from 11 December.

summary.en: A student research conference on art and culture at Tbilisi State University on 26-27 December 2026, open to bachelor's and master's students and recent graduates from any university. Abstracts of up to 300 words are due by 10 November 2026.
summary.ka: სტუდენტური სამეცნიერო კონფერენცია ხელოვნებასა და კულტურაზე თბილისის სახელმწიფო უნივერსიტეტში 2026 წლის 26-27 დეკემბერს, ღიაა ნებისმიერი უნივერსიტეტის ბაკალავრებისთვის, მაგისტრანტებისა და ახალი კურსდამთავრებულებისთვის. 300 სიტყვამდე თეზისების მიღება 2026 წლის 10 ნოემბრამდე გრძელდება.
summary.ar: مؤتمر بحثي طلابي حول الفن والثقافة في جامعة تبليسي الحكومية يومي 26-27 ديسمبر 2026، مفتوح لطلاب البكالوريوس والماجستير والخريجين الجدد من أي جامعة. آخر موعد لتقديم الملخصات (حتى 300 كلمة) هو 10 نوفمبر 2026.

about.en:
The Institute of the History and Theory of Art at Ivane Javakhishvili Tbilisi State University is holding the student conference 'Man and Culture Across Epochs' at TSU on 26-27 December 2026. The programme will be published from 11 December.

It is open to bachelor's and master's students and recent graduates from any university. Applicants email an abstract of up to 300 words (with name, year of study and field before the text; Sylfaen 12, 1.5 spacing) plus a written recommendation from a supervisor. Each accepted paper gets a 15-minute slot and 5 minutes of questions. The working language is Georgian.

For students of art history, cultural studies, history or humanities it is an accessible first conference presentation, with a short abstract and a quick turnaround.

en: Open to students from any university
Short 300-word abstract
15-minute presentations with Q&A

eligibility.en: Bachelor's and master's students and recent graduates from any university who can present in Georgian. A supervisor's recommendation is required.

en: Write an abstract of up to 300 words; put your name, year of study and field before the text
Get a written recommendation or conclusion from your supervisor
Email both to tsuarthistoryconference@gmail.com by 10 November 2026

about.en:
TSU's Faculty of Humanities holds its ninth student conference on 17-18 December 2026 to support student research, interdisciplinary work and interest in Georgian studies. Sections include history, ethnology, archaeology, Georgian studies, Caucasology, translation studies, Western European languages and literature, American studies, oriental studies, Slavic and Russian studies, philosophy, cultural studies, art and interdisciplinary research.

Applicants email an application and a one-page abstract (max. 250 words, Sylfaen 12, 1.5 spacing) with a written statement from a professor or supervisor. Presentations are in person: 15 minutes plus 5 minutes of discussion, in Georgian.

It is a low-stakes, well-organised setting for humanities students to give their first conference paper.

about.en:
The youth movement 'Davitianni', in cooperation with St. Andrew the First-Called Georgian University (SANGU) in Tbilisi, is running the university intellectual olympiad 'Get to Know Abkhazia, Protect the Heritage'. Registration is open until 6 November 2026 through the form linked on SANGU's announcement.

The olympiad has three stages: a team qualifying round in crossword format (teams of 2-3 students), an individual round with a test, and a team final that decides first, second and third places. Every participant receives a certificate and scholarship points, and the winning teams go on to compete in a grand final on behalf of SANGU.

It suits SANGU students who enjoy quiz-style competitions and Georgian history, and offers scholarship points as a tangible reward.

about.en:
Tbilisi State University's Library runs a children's events series, 'University Library for Children'. Its next event is a conference for pupils of public and private schools in Georgia dedicated to the 100th anniversary of the birth of the Georgian writer Revaz Inanishvili, with presentations on his work.

Pupils submit an abstract of up to 250 words (one A4 page, Sylfaen 12, 1.5 spacing) by 9 November 2026. Selected authors are told by 16 November and send their final papers by 1 December; the conference date will be announced afterwards. The working language is Georgian, and the email must name the pupil, the school and the supervising teacher.

It gives secondary-school students a rare chance to present literary research at a university, which is good preparation for academic writing and a strong line on a university application.
